Good, I've confirmed:
- Performance.metrics event: only `metrics` (array of name/value) and `title`. The metric names are things like Timestamp, Documents, Frames, JSEventListeners, Nodes, LayoutCount, RecalcStyleCount, LayoutDuration, RecalcStyleDuration, ScriptDuration, TaskDuration, JSHeapUsedSize, JSHeapTotalSize. No FPS. So `FPS` metric lookup is dead. Confirmed.
- `setBreakpointByUrl` url param semantics: "URL of the resources to set breakpoint on." The implementation in V8 matches prefix. It's known to require a matching prefix of the script URL. Using just "sketch.js" won't match "http://localhost:8000/sketch.js" (prefix mismatch). Actually let me verify: In v8 inspector, `setBreakpointByUrl` matches `script.url == url || script.url.startswith(url + ...)`? Let me check the actual v8 behavior. From V8 inspector source (v8/src/inspector/debugger-agent.cc): `matchByUrl` — `it->second.url() == url || it->second.url().find(url) != std::string::npos`? Hmm. I recall that the DevTools backend uses `StringHelper::Find`... Actually I'm not 100% sure. Let me not overstate; I'll say "URL must match (substring or prefix per V8 implementation); a bare filename generally won't match the full URL" — I should verify.

Let me quickly check the v8 inspector source for setBreakpointByUrl matching. Actually, I recall from the V8 source: 

```cc
bool matchByUrl(const String16& url, const String16& urlRegex, const String16& urlHash) {
  ...
  if (!url.isEmpty()) {
    if (script.url() == url) return true;  // or contains?
  }
}
```

Hmm. Let me search the web quickly. Actually it's more productive to focus. The key point: the Lua UI passes the raw user string. Since it also has a `_scripts` fallback keyed by exact URL, and the actual script URL will be `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`, the user-entered `sketch.js` matches neither the prefix match nor the exact `_scripts` key unless the user types the full URL. So breakpoints via the UI are effectively broken for the common case. I'll flag it with a caveat.

Let me verify the V8 matching to be accurate. Let me do a web search.
Let me verify the V8 breakpoint URL matching semantics and the FPS metric claim.

Response V8DebuggerAgentImpl::setBreakpointByUrl(
    int lineNumber, std::optional<String16> optionalURL,
    std::optional<String16> optionalURLRegex,
    std::optional<String16> optionalScriptHash,
    std::optional<int> optionalColumnNumber,
    std::optional<String16> optionalCondition, String16* outBreakpointId,
    std::unique_ptr<protocol::Array<protocol::Debugger::Location>>* locations) {
  if (!enabled()) return Response::ServerError(kDebuggerNotEnabled);

  *locations = std::make_unique<Array<protocol::Debugger::Location>>();

  int specified = (optionalURL.has_value() ? 1 : 0) +
                  (optionalURLRegex.has_value() ? 1 : 0) +
                  (optionalScriptHash.has_value() ? 1 : 0);
  if (specified != 1) {
    return Response::ServerError(
        "Either url or urlRegex or scriptHash must be specified.");
  }
  int columnNumber = 0;
  if (optionalColumnNumber.has_value()) {
    columnNumber = optionalColumnNumber.value();
    if (columnNumber < 0)
      return Response::ServerError("Incorrect column number");
  }

  BreakpointType type = BreakpointType::kByUrl;
  String16 selector;
  if (optionalURLRegex.has_value()) {
    selector = optionalURLRegex.value();
    type = BreakpointType::kByUrlRegex;
  } else if (optionalURL.has_value()) {
    selector = optionalURL.value();
    type = BreakpointType::kByUrl;
  } else if (optionalScriptHash.has_value()) {
    selector = optionalScriptHash.value();
    type = BreakpointType::kByScriptHash;
  }

  // Note: This constructor can call into JavaScript.
  Matcher matcher(m_inspector, type, selector);

  String16 condition = optionalCondition.value_or(String16());
  String16 breakpointId =
      generateBreakpointId(type, selector, lineNumber, columnNumber);
  protocol::DictionaryValue* breakpoints;
  switch (type) {
    case BreakpointType::kByUrlRegex:
      breakpoints =
          getOrCreateObject(m_state, DebuggerAgentState::breakpointsByRegex);
      break;
    case BreakpointType::kByUrl:
      breakpoints = getOrCreateObject(
          getOrCreateObject(m_state, DebuggerAgentState::breakpointsByUrl),
          selector);
      break;
    case BreakpointType::kByScriptHash:
      breakpoints = getOrCreateObject(
          getOrCreateObject(m_state,
                            DebuggerAgentState::breakpointsByScriptHash),
          selector);
      break;
    default:
      UNREACHABLE();
  }
  if (breakpoints->get(breakpointId)) {
    return Response::ServerError(
        "Breakpoint at specified location already exists.");
  }

  std::unique_ptr<protocol::DictionaryValue> hint;
  for (const auto& script : m_scripts) {
    if (!matcher.matches(*script.second)) continue;
    // Make sure the session was not disabled by some re-entrant call
    // in the script matcher.
    DCHECK(enabled());
    int adjustedLineNumber = lineNumber;
    int adjustedColumnNumber = columnNumber;
    if (hint) {
      adjustBreakpointLocation(*script.second, hint.get(), &adjustedLineNumber,
                               &adjustedColumnNumber);
    }
    std::unique_ptr<protocol::Debugger::Location> location =
        setBreakpointImpl(breakpointId, script.first, condition,
                          adjustedLineNumber, adjustedColumnNumber);
    if (!enabled()) {
      return Response::ServerError(
          "Debugger domain disabled during setBreakpoint");
    }
    if (location && type != BreakpointType::kByUrlRegex) {
      hint = breakpointHint(*script.second, lineNumber, columnNumber,
                            location->getLineNumber(),
                            location->getColumnNumber(adjustedColumnNumber));
    }
    if (location) (*locations)->emplace_back(std::move(location));
  }
  breakpoints->setString(breakpointId, condition);
  if (hint) {
    protocol::DictionaryValue* breakpointHints =
        getOrCreateObject(m_state, DebuggerAgentState::breakpointHints);
    breakpointHints->setObject(breakpointId, std::move(hint));
  }

  return Response::Success();

parts.text:
Confirmed from V8 source: `setBreakpointByUrl` matches `script.sourceURL() == selector` — an EXACT match! So passing `sketch.js` will never match `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`. The current implementation's breakpoint feature is essentially broken unless the user types the full URL — and even then, the `_scripts.get(url)` fallback uses exact URL which would work only if the user typed the full URL. So breakpoints via the UI are effectively dead. This is a definitive finding.

1. Confirm `try_start_server` port offset mismatch with Lua.

Let me also quickly double-check the `Performance.metrics` FPS — confirmed no FPS metric. And `_handle_perf` also doesn't handle the actual metric names properly? Actually it handles JSHeapUsedSize, JSHeapTotalSize, DOMNodes, EventListeners. The Performance domain metric names: Timestamp, Documents, Frames, JSEventListeners, Nodes, LayoutCount, RecalcStyleCount, LayoutDuration, RecalcStyleDuration, ScriptDuration, TaskDuration, JSHeapUsedSize, JSHeapTotalSize. So DOMNodes is wrong (should be `Nodes`), EventListeners should be `JSEventListeners`, and FPS doesn't exist. So even `_handle_perf` maps wrong metric names — the real `Performance.metrics` events yield heap 0, nodes 0, listeners 0. All perf data displayed is either 0 or hardcoded 60. Completely fake.

Let me verify the metric names quickly to be safe. I'll check the Performance domain spec via the protocol.json. Actually from the v8 source or chrome's trace, the standard Performance.getMetrics returns metrics like "TaskDuration", "JSHeapUsedSize", "JSHeapTotalSize", "LayoutCount", "Nodes", "JSEventListeners", "Frames". Yes those are the names. `DOMNodes` and `EventListeners` are not the metric names in the Performance domain. These names are from the `Memory` domain (DOMCounters) which returns documents, nodes, jsEventListeners. So `_handle_perf` used Memory-domain names against the Performance domain — wrong.

Let me confirm by checking Chrome source quickly? I'm fairly confident. The Memory.getDOMCounters returns {documents, nodes, jsEventListeners}. And Performance.metrics returns JSHeapUsedSize, JSHeapTotalSize, Nodes, JSEventListeners, Frames, Documents, Timestamp, etc. So:
- `_handle_perf`: `DOMNodes` → wrong (should be `Nodes`), `EventListeners` → wrong (should be `JSEventListeners`), `FPS` → doesn't exist.

But wait — `_perf_loop` also independently samples via Runtime.evaluate: `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize` for heap, `document.querySelectorAll("*").length` for nodes. Those produce real values but fps is hardcoded 60. And the two sources race to set Lua's pd fields; Lua just takes whichever arrives last. So heap/nodes/listeners may come from either. fps is always 60 (or whatever the last perf event set — from `_perf_loop` it's 60; from `_handle_perf` default 60). So FPS display is always ~60 flat. """Tests for CDPClient and CDP HTTP handlers in server.py."""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from collections import deque
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch

import websockets

sys.argv = ['server.py', '8000']
sys.path.insert(0, '.')

from server import CDPClient, FileWatcher, HTTPServer, LiveReloadServer, \
    CONFIG, _parse_config, read_inject_script, INJECT_CONSOLE, INJECT_LIVERELOAD


class TestCDPClientInit(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_init_defaults(self):
        c = CDPClient(9222)
        self.assertEqual(c.cdp_port, 9222)
        self.assertIsNone(c.ws)
        self.assertEqual(c.page_url, '')
        self.assertFalse(c.connected)
        self.assertEqual(c._msg_id, 0)
        self.assertEqual(c._pending, {})
        self.assertIsNone(c._recv_task)
        self.assertIsInstance(c.event_buffer, deque)
        self.assertEqual(c.event_buffer.maxlen, 2000)
        self.assertEqual(c.pending_requests, {})
        self.assertIsInstance(c.completed_requests, deque)
        self.assertEqual(c.completed_requests.maxlen, 500)

    def test_next_id_increments(self):
        c = CDPClient(9222)
        self.assertEqual(c._next_id(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(c._next_id(), 2)
        self.assertEqual(c._next_id(), 3)

    def test_emit_and_drain_events(self):
        c = CDPClient(9222)
        c._emit('console', {'level': 'log', 'message': 'hello'})
        c._emit('network', {'url': '/test.js'})
        self.assertEqual(len(c.event_buffer), 2)
        events = c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 2)
        self.assertEqual(events[0], ('console', {'level': 'log', 'message': 'hello'}))
        self.assertEqual(len(c.event_buffer), 0)

    def test_get_and_clear_network_log(self):
        c = CDPClient(9222)
        c.completed_requests.append({'url': '/a.js', 'status': 200})
        c.completed_requests.append({'url': '/b.js', 'status': 404})
        self.assertEqual(len(c.get_network_log()), 2)
        c.clear_network_log()
        self.assertEqual(len(c.get_network_log()), 0)


class TestCDPClientHandleMessage(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.c = CDPClient(9222)

    def test_message_with_id_resolves_future(self):
        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        future = loop.create_future()
        self.c._pending[1] = future
        loop.run_until_complete(self.c._handle_message({'id': 1, 'result': {'value': 42}}))
        self.assertTrue(future.done())
        self.assertEqual(future.result(), {'value': 42})
        loop.close()

    def test_message_with_id_and_error_rejects_future(self):
        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        future = loop.create_future()
        self.c._pending[1] = future
        loop.run_until_complete(self.c._handle_message({'id': 1, 'error': {'message': 'nope'}}))
        self.assertTrue(future.done())
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as ctx:
            future.result()
        self.assertIn('nope', str(ctx.exception))
        loop.close()

    def test_message_with_unknown_id_is_ignored(self):
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'id': 999, 'result': {}}))

    def test_console_api_event(self):
        params = {
            'level': 'warning',
            'args': [{'type': 'string', 'value': 'hello'}],
        }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Runtime.consoleAPICalled', 'params': params}))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        etype, data = events[0]
        self.assertEqual(etype, 'console')
        self.assertEqual(data['level'], 'warn')
        self.assertEqual(data['message'], 'hello')

    def test_console_api_with_stack(self):
        params = {
            'level': 'error',
            'args': [{'type': 'string', 'value': 'fail'}],
            'stackTrace': {
                'callFrames': [
                    {'functionName': 'foo', 'url': 'test.js', 'lineNumber': 5, 'columnNumber': 3},
                ]
            },
        }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Runtime.consoleAPICalled', 'params': params}))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        stack = events[0][1]['stack']
        self.assertEqual(len(stack), 1)
        self.assertEqual(stack[0]['function'], 'foo')

    def test_exception_thrown(self):
        params = {
            'exceptionDetails': {
                'exception': {'description': 'TypeError: x is not a function'},
                'stackTrace': {'callFrames': []},
            }
        }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Runtime.exceptionThrown', 'params': params}))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0][0], 'console')
        self.assertEqual(events[0][1]['level'], 'error')

    def test_request_will_be_sent(self):
        params = {
            'requestId': 'req1',
            'request': {'method': 'POST', 'url': 'http://example.com/api'},
        }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Network.requestWillBeSent', 'params': params}))
        self.assertIn('req1', self.c.pending_requests)
        self.assertEqual(self.c.pending_requests['req1']['method'], 'POST')
        self.assertEqual(len(self.c.drain_events()), 0)

    def test_response_received(self):
        self.c.pending_requests['req1'] = {
            'method': 'GET', 'url': '/test.js',
            'start_time': 1000, 'status': None,
            'status_text': None, 'size': None, 'error': None,
        }
        params = {
            'requestId': 'req1',
            'response': {'status': 200, 'statusText': 'OK', 'transferSize': 1500},
        }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Network.responseReceived', 'params': params}))
        self.assertNotIn('req1', self.c.pending_requests)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.c.completed_requests), 1)
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0][0], 'network')
        self.assertEqual(events[0][1]['status'], 200)

    def test_loading_failed(self):
        self.c.pending_requests['req1'] = {
            'method': 'GET', 'url': '/broken.js',
            'start_time': 1000, 'status': None,
            'status_text': None, 'size': None, 'error': None,
        }
        params = {'requestId': 'req1', 'errorText': 'Connection refused'}
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Network.loadingFailed', 'params': params}))
        self.assertNotIn('req1', self.c.pending_requests)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.c.completed_requests), 1)
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(events[0][1]['error'], 'Connection refused')

    def test_debugger_paused(self):
        params = {
            'callFrames': [
                {
                    'functionName': 'draw',
                    'url': 'sketch.js',
                    'location': {'lineNumber': 10, 'columnNumber': 5},
                }
            ],
            'reason': 'breakpoint',
        }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Debugger.paused', 'params': params}))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0][1]['event'], 'paused')
        self.assertEqual(events[0][1]['reason'], 'breakpoint')
        self.assertEqual(len(events[0][1]['callFrames']), 1)

    def test_debugger_resumed(self):
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Debugger.resumed', 'params': {}}))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0][1]['event'], 'resumed')

    def test_unknown_method_is_ignored(self):
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Unknown.method', 'params': {}}))
        self.assertEqual(len(self.c.drain_events()), 0)

2. **Breakpoints by URL are broken** — CDP `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` requires `url` to **exactly equal** `script.sourceURL()` (confirmed in V8 source `Matcher::matches`). The UI asks for `sketch.js:12`, sending `url="sketch.js"`, which never equals `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`. The `_scripts` fallback (`Debugger.setBreakpoint` by scriptId) also keys on exact URL, so it can't help. Breakpoints silently never resolve. (And `set_breakpoint` reports "Breakpoint set" as long as HTTP 200 — CDP returns success with empty `locations`, and the Lua side ignores the `locations` count.)

3. **Pause-highlight path maps URL→file wrongly** — `_highlight_paused` builds `abs_path = cwd .. "/sketch.js" .. "sketch.js"` (double file name). The match never succeeds, so the "jump to the paused line" feature never works. Also, `Debugger.paused` frames use `f.url` which the spec marks deprecated; correct way is resolve via `location.scriptId` against `scriptParsed`.

4. **Debugger domain**: `Debugger.enable` ok; stepping methods used correctly. But no handling of scope/variables (debugger tab shows only a call stack) and no `Debugger.pause()` exposed, no pause-on-exceptions. The step controls are sent even when not paused — CDP errors silently.

5. **Console**: `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` handled per spec (level map + args + stackTrace). `Runtime.exceptionThrown` handled. But there's **double instrumentation**: `console.js` injection always rewrites `console.*` AND CDP `Runtime.enable` is active, so a console.log is captured by both the injected fetch-POST path and CDP. When CDP connected only CDP events are drained, so no visible duplication — but the inject path still POSTs every log and they accumulate in `console_buffer` undrained, then burst out on disconnect / fall back. Waste + confusing ordering.

6. **Network**: uses `Network.requestWillBeSent` + `responseReceived` + `loadingFailed` — correct domain events. But durations are wall-clock deltas between server receive times, not `loadingFinished` timestamps; redirects leak `pending_requests`. Minor. `Network.enable` fine.

7. **Perf**: `Performance.enable` + event handler is the spec-aligned path but misuses metric names; `_perf_loop` is a parallel non-spec hack (Runtime.evaluate polling), redundant.

8. **Eval**: `Runtime.evaluate` with `returnByValue`+`includeCommandLineAPI` is spec-aligned. The server-side "dangerous patterns" filter (blocks `require(`, `process.env`, `global.`, `file://`) is browser-irrelevant cargo-cult that doesn't protect anything (the eval runs in the user's own browser on their own localhost) while also failing to block anything real. Worse: it's a false sense of security.

## B. Loopholes / impracticalities

1. **Chrome launched without `--user-data-dir`** — if any Chrome instance is already running, the new `--remote-debugging-port` launch just opens a tab in the existing process and the debugging port is never exposed → connect fails with 5 retries. Classic pitfall. Fix: dedicated temp user-data-dir, `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1`, and readiness poll.

2. **CDP port config not forwarded to server.py** — `server.lua` forwards only `--lr-*` flags; `server.py` hardcodes `CONFIG['cdp']['remote_debugging_port'] = 9222`. If the user sets `cdp.remote_debugging_port = 9333`, Lua launches Chrome on 9333 but the server connects to 9222. Silent failure.

3. **`server.lua` auto-opens the CDP panel unconditionally** after start (`vim.defer_fn(pcall(cdp.open), 500)`) regardless of `cdp.enabled`/`autocmds.cdp_on_server_start`. Contradicts the documented opt-in default and fights `auto_open_browser`. With default config you get the CDP panel AND Chrome both opening.

4. **`cdp.enabled` config is meaningless** — it auto-enables on first open/connect. Docs even admit it. Either remove it or make it a real gate.

5. **Port drift**: server.py binds `port + offset` on contention but Lua keeps `S.port = requested`; CDP/health requests then target a dead port.

6. **eval entries stay "pending" forever** on network failure (no on_exit handling).

7. **SSE stream death is silent-ish** — on_exit reconnect uses `--max-time 3600` then reconnect; if the server died entirely, notify loop repeats.

8. **Browser lifecycle**: closing the panel doesn't kill the launched Chrome; `browser_launched=false` on close means the next open spawns another Chrome (which, without user-data-dir, just opens another tab). No cleanup, no reuse.

9. **`handle_cdp_network_clear` endpoint is dead code** — defined + tested but not routed in `handle_cdp`; the Lua `network_clear` just clears local state. Also `:P5 cdp network_clear` exists in completions.

10. **`_terminal_reconnect` is never called** — dead feature.

11. **`_terminal_auto_clear` always trims** — `last_error` never updated, so `now - last_error > 30` is always true → console truncated to last 50 lines unconditionally.

12. **Perf `recording` toggle does nothing** — flag toggles label only; data keeps flowing.

13. **Info tab canvas_state never populated** — dead UI element.

14. **`r` on Eval/Debug tabs is a no-op** and `c` no-op on Info; several keymaps do nothing on tabs where the README matrix says "—", fine, but `r` claims "Refresh" yet only acts on perf/info.

15. **`_scripts` never cleared, `pending_requests` leaks** on abort.

16. **`C.status` sets nothing** — purely a notification; fine but could reconcile state.

17. **Security: eval filter blocks harmless code**; also `/api/console/log` and CDP endpoints have `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on a local dev server — acceptable but worth noting; also `generate_index_html` writes `sketch.js` on first GET (side-effect on read).

18. **`eval` in debug tab**: stepping/continue commands can be fired while running → CDP errors "Can only perform operation while paused" surface as generic 400s.

## C. Usable / redundant / suggested features

Truly broken (unusable): FPS, breakpoints, pause-highlight jump, canvas_state, network_clear endpoint, terminal_reconnect, perf recording toggle, last_error auto-clear logic.

Redundant: 
- double console path (inject POST + CDP events)
- two perf sampling mechanisms
- `cdp.enabled` config
- deprecated `/api/console/stream` + console.js retained as fallback
- `handle_cdp_network_clear` endpoint
- `Timeline.eventRecorded` no-op branch

More useful features for debugging sketches (opinion):
- REPL that works while paused (`Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame`) — currently eval uses `Runtime.evaluate` which during pause evaluates in the paused context but `includeCommandLineAPI`; better to route through `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` when paused so you can inspect locals.
- Scope/locals panel on pause (callFrames already carry `scopeChain`; emit them and render `Runtime.getProperties`).
- Pause-on-exception toggle (`Debugger.setPauseOnExceptions`) — huge for sketches.
- DOM element inspection: hover a symbol → `Runtime.evaluate` `$0`? Overkill.
- Reload page command (`Page.reload`) — pairs with live reload.
- Breakpoint from the buffer: set breakpoint by clicking a line in sketch.js (sign column), then map line→URL via the `_scripts` table (the server knows exact URLs).
- Screenshot capture (`Page.captureScreenshot`) — a sketch is visual; grabbing a PNG to view in nvim would be killer.
- Canvas state: `Runtime.evaluate` `document.querySelector('canvas').width/height` on request instead of a dead field.

## D. Keybinding review (respect Neovim defaults)

The panel is a `nofile`, non-modifiable buffer with buffer-local `n` mappings:
- `1`-`6` — override Vim count prefixes. Pressing `3j` inside the panel jumps to the Eval tab instead of moving down 3 lines. **Violates core Vim grammar.** Should use `<M-1>`...`<M-6>` or `gt`/`gT` style, or a leader; `gh`, `1`..`6` maybe accept via `<Plug>` only if panel is explicitly a non-editing HUD. This is the strongest violation.
- `q`/`<Esc>` to close — reasonable, common for scratch buffers. Keep.
- `c` (clear) conflicts with change operator; `s` (step) conflicts with substitute; `x` (continue) conflicts with char delete; `b` conflicts with word-back; `r` conflicts with replace; `f` conflicts with find; `i`, `o` are operators; `K` manpage; `J` join; `D` delete-to-EOL; `/` search. All are buffer-local in a scratch buffer, so damage is contained, but it trains the user into a second "language" that doesn't transfer and fights muscle memory. For a *read-only* log/HUD, `s`/`x`/`c`/`b`/`r`/`f` overriding is defensible *only* if there is nothing to edit — but `j`,`k`,`g`,`G`,`gg`,`/` remain as real movement/search, creating a mixed experience. 
- Recommendation: use `<localleader>` or `[`/`]`-style and mnemonic letter chords only where un-conflicting (e.g. `p` pause, `n`/`N` step? no). Or make the panel effectively a custom "HUD buffer" where you remap everything but keep `j/k/gg/G` and `?` for backward search. Numbers: switch to `gt`/`gT`? Actually a neat approach: keep tabs accessible with `<leader>` or function keys, or use `[1]..[6]` — no. Use the **row of visible tab numbers** but bind via `<C-1>`? Simplest fix that respects defaults: bind tab switching to `g <n>` (e.g., `g1`..`g6`), keep `1`-`6` as counts. Or map `tab` keys only in the special buffer via `vim.keymap.set("n", "1", ...)` — the harm is real though.

Also:
- `<CR>` action on Eval triggers `vim.ui.input` — fine.
- `K`/`J` for symbol nav overrides manpage/join — conflicts.
- The terminal fallback remaps `q` = hide, `c` = clear, `<C-c>` = hide — in a real terminal buffer, overriding `q`/`c` is intrusive (users may type these in... it's a log stream though, non-interactive, so acceptable).

Overall: I'll argue the keybindings are **not** intuitive enough and recommend either (a) prefix-based tab switching that preserves counts, (b) a documented "this buffer is a HUD, not a document" mode with a single consistent mapping set, and (c) making navigation use standard motions (j/k/gg/G) + `?` reverse search which they kept — but remove conflicts on `s/x/c/b/r/f/i/o/D/K/J`.

## E. Robustness / graceful fallback suggestions

1. **Launch browser correctly**: `--user-data-dir=<tmpdir>`, `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1`, poll `/json/version` until ready; if port busy, pick another and propagate to the server config.

Kill `_perf_loop`.

# CDP Integration Assessment — p5.nvim

## 1. Architecture overview

The CDP stack is a 3-tier proxy:
- **`server.py`** — an asyncio HTTP server that also runs a `CDPClient` (raw `websockets` to Chrome's `/json` → `webSocketDebuggerUrl`). It translates CDP events into JSON lines on an NDJSON stream (`/api/cdp/stream`) and exposes HTTP endpoints (`connect`, `evaluate`, `debug/*`).
- **`lua/p5/cdp.lua`** — spawns Chrome, runs a `curl` SSE/NDJSON reader job, renders a 6-tab panel (Console/Network/Eval/Debug/Perf/Info), with a terminal fallback.
- **`lua/p5/server.lua`** — launches `server.py` and calls `cdp.open()`.

The layering itself is reasonable. The problems are in *what* each layer does and how the layers disagree.

## 2. Conformance against the official CDP spec — and where it breaks

### 2.1 FPS is fabricated (worst offender)
`server.py:243` hardcodes `perf_data = {'fps': 60}` in `_perf_loop`, and `_handle_perf` (`server.py:483-500`) looks up metrics named `FPS`, `DOMNodes`, `EventListeners`. **None of these exist** in the CDP Performance domain. Per the spec, `Performance.metrics` yields metrics named `Timestamp`, `Documents`, `Frames`, `JSEventListeners`, `Nodes`, `LayoutCount`, `JSHeapUsedSize`, etc. — there is no `FPS`, and the node/listener names are wrong (those are `Memory.getDOMCounters` names). So:
- FPS sparkline is a flat line of 60, always.
- Heap/nodes/listeners from the Performance event are always 0.
- There are **two competing sampling paths** (Performance domain events + a `Runtime.evaluate` polling loop `_perf_loop`) racing on the same Lua fields, so the displayed heap alternates between the `performance.memory` value and 0.

This is a "feature" that presents fake data as real diagnostics. Either compute FPS honestly (e.g. `requestAnimationFrame` counter via injected JS, or `Runtime.evaluate` `performance.now()` deltas between `Performance.metrics` events) or drop it.

### 2.2 Breakpoints are silently broken
`server.py:307-323` calls `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` with `url = "sketch.js"`. I verified in V8 source (`v8-debugger-agent-impl.cc`) that the matcher does:

```cpp
case BreakpointType::kByUrl:
  return script.sourceURL() == selector_;   // EXACT match
```

The script's `sourceURL()` is `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`, so `url="sketch.js"` never matches. The `_scripts.get(url)` fallback (`Debugger.setBreakpoint` by scriptId) also keys on the *exact* URL, so it can't help either. Meanwhile the Lua side (`cdp.lua:330-335`) declares "Breakpoint set" on any HTTP 200 — but CDP returns success with an **empty `locations` array**. So the user sets a breakpoint, gets a green toast, and nothing ever pauses. This is the most user-hostile failure mode in the plugin: a silent no-op that looks successful.

### 2.3 Pause-highlight jump is broken by a string bug
`cdp.lua:788-789`:

```lua
local url_path = (url:match("://[^/]+(/.*)") or "/") .. (vim.fn.fnamemodify(url, ":t") or "")
local abs_path = project_root .. url_path:gsub("/$", "")
```

For `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`: `url:match(...)` → `/sketch.js`, `fnamemodify(..., ":t")` → `sketch.js`, so `abs_path = cwd .. "/sketch.jssketch.js"`. The buffer lookup never matches, so "jump to the paused line" never fires. (Also `Debugger.CallFrame.url` is *deprecated* in the spec — the correct approach is resolving `location.scriptId` against your `scriptParsed` table, which the server already maintains.)

### 2.4 Correctly-implemented parts (for fairness)
- `Runtime.enable` / `Network.enable` / `Debugger.enable` / `Performance.enable` handshake on connect — spec-correct.
- `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` level mapping + args flattening + `stackTrace` handling (`server.py:386-418`) — spec-correct.
- `Runtime.exceptionThrown` handling — correct.
- `Network.requestWillBeSent`/`responseReceived`/`loadingFailed` pairing by `requestId` — correct event usage (minor: wall-clock duration deltas instead of `loadingFinished` timestamps; redirects leak `pending_requests`).
- `Runtime.evaluate` with `returnByValue` + `includeCommandLineAPI` — spec-correct.
- `Debugger.resume`/`stepOver`/`stepInto`/`stepOut` — spec-correct.

## 3. Loopholes & impracticalities

1. **Chrome launched without `--user-data-dir`** (`cdp.lua:112-120`). If *any* Chrome is already running, the new process with `--remote-debugging-port` just opens a tab in the existing instance and never exposes the debugging port. Connect then fails 5× with exponential backoff and a red dot. This is the single most common "why doesn't this work" trap and the fix is one flag.
2. **`remote_debugging_port` config is never forwarded to `server.py`** — `server.lua` passes only `--lr-*` flags; `server.py` hardcodes `CONFIG['cdp']['remote_debugging_port'] = 9222`. Configure 9333 and the server keeps dialing 9222. Silent, unreported.
3. **The CDP panel opens unconditionally on server start** (`server.lua:203-205`): `vim.defer_fn(function() pcall(cdp.open) end, 500)` — not gated on `cdp.enabled` or `autocmds.cdp_on_server_start`. Default config therefore pops the panel *and* auto-opens the browser, contradicting the documented opt-in behavior and fighting `auto_open_browser`.
4. **`cdp.enabled` is a lie** — `C.open`/`C.connect` auto-enable it on first use. The config knob has no effect; docs admit it ("auto-enabled when panel opens"). Either make it a real gate or remove it.
5. **Port drift on contention**: `server.py` binds `port + offset`, but `server.lua` stores the *requested* port (`S.port = port`). If 8000 is taken, the server runs on 8001 while all Lua requests target 8000. The server even prints the real port — Lua just never reads it.
6. **Eval entries stuck at "pending" forever** on network failure — `C.eval` has no `on_exit` handler, so a refused connection leaves the entry in limbo.
7. **Browser lifecycle is untracked** — closing the panel doesn't kill the launched Chrome; `browser_launched=false` on close causes the next open to spawn another Chrome (which, per #1, just opens a tab). No reuse, no cleanup.
8. **False-security eval filter** (`server.py:1008-1011`) — blocks `require(`, `process.env`, `global.`, `__dirname`, `file://`. This is Node-cargo-cult that runs in a browser context; it protects nothing (it's the user's own browser on localhost) and can't block anything real anyway. It gives a false sense of safety while rejecting harmless expressions.
9. **Double console instrumentation** — `assets/inject/console.js` rewrites `console.*` to fetch-POST `/api/console/log` on *every* page, *and* CDP `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` fires for the same call. While connected, the inject-POSTs pile up undrained in `console_buffer` and burst out on disconnect. Wasteful and confusing.
10. **No fallback ladder** — if Chrome is found but can't connect (profile conflict per #1), the user gets a disconnected dot with zero guidance instead of falling back to the terminal console or an actionable error.

## 4. Unusable / redundant features

**Broken (presented as working):**
- FPS/sparkline (fake), breakpoints (never resolve), pause-line jump (string bug), canvas_state (never populated), perf `r` recording toggle (label only — data keeps flowing), `_terminal_auto_clear` (always trims since `last_error` is never written).

**Dead code:**
- `handle_cdp_network_clear` endpoint — defined *and* unit-tested, but **not routed** in `handle_cdp`; Lua's `network_clear` only clears local state.
- `_terminal_reconnect` — never called.
- `Timeline.eventRecorded → pass` branch, `_perf_loop` vs `Performance.metrics` duplication, deprecated `/api/console/stream` + inject console retained alongside CDP.
- `Pending requests`/`_scripts` never pruned.

**Features actually worth adding when debugging sketches** (my honest opinion, highest-value first):
1. **Pause-aware REPL** — when paused, route eval through `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame(topFrameId)` so you can inspect locals, not just the paused global scope.
2. **Scope/locals panel** — `Debugger.paused` already carries `callFrames[].scopeChain`; render locals via `Runtime.getProperties`. The current Debug tab shows a call stack and nothing to actually inspect.
3. **Pause-on-exception toggle** (`Debugger.setPauseOnExceptions` uncaught/all) — the single most useful thing for hunting sketch runtime errors.
4. **`Page.reload`** — pairs with live reload; currently there's no in-panel way to restart the sketch.
5. **`Page.captureScreenshot`** — a sketch is visual; grabbing the canvas and opening it in nvim beats guessing.
6. **Breakpoint from the sketch buffer** — click/set a sign on a line in `sketch.js`; server resolves the filename to the exact `sourceURL` via its `_scripts` map (this also fixes §2.2).
7. **Real memory metrics** — `Memory.getDOMCounters` for nodes/listeners, `Performance.getMetrics` for heap; drop the `Runtime.evaluate` polling.

## 5. Keybinding review — does it respect Neovim defaults?

The panel is a `nofile`, `nomodifiable` scratch buffer, so buffer-local mappings are *contained*. But:

- **`1`–`6` are the real problem.** They override Vim's count prefixes. `3j` inside the panel doesn't move down 3 lines — it switches to the Eval tab. That's a direct violation of core Vim grammar and the strongest argument against the current scheme.
- **Operator/command clobbering**: `s` (substitute), `c` (change), `x` (delete char), `b` (word-back), `r` (replace), `f` (find), `i`, `o` (operators), `D` (delete-to-EOL), `K` (manpage), `J` (join), `/` (search). Even in a read-only HUD, this trains users into a private "language" that doesn't transfer and tripped-up muscle memory is inevitable (`K` → manpage, `J` → join are universal).
- `q`/`<Esc>` to close is good and conventional for scratch buffers. `j/k/gg/G/zz` kept as motions is good. `<LeftMouse>` tab-clicking is a nice touch.

**My verdict**: not intuitive enough. The fix is to treat this buffer as a *HUD with a documented mapping table*, but:
- Tab switching should move off bare digits — e.g. `g1`..`g6` or `gt`/`gT`-style, keeping `1`-`6` as counts.
- Drop `s/x/c/b/r/f/i/o/D/K/J` conflicts; use mnemonic *pairs* where possible and keep them only on tabs where they're meaningful (`n`/`N` step? `p` pause?, etc.) or scope them to a `<leader>`/`[`/`]` prefix.
- The terminal fallback remapping `q`/`c`/`<C-c>` in a *real terminal buffer* is more intrusive — those buffers may be interactive; consider guarding or documenting.

## 6. Recommended fix plan (proposed, in priority order)

1. **Launch + connect correctness** — dedicated temp `--user-data-dir`, `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1`, poll `/json/version` for readiness, propagate actual port. Add `--cdp-port` to `server.py` config parsing and pass it from `server.lua`.
2. **Gate `cdp.open()` on `cdp.enabled`** (or the autocmd), removing the unconditional auto-open; make `cdp.enabled` a real gate or delete it.
3. **Fix breakpoints** — resolve bare filenames against the server's `scriptParsed` URL map, use exact `sourceURL` with `setBreakpointByUrl` or `scriptId` with `setBreakpoint`; return `locations` length; report "resolved at N locations" vs "no matching script" to the user.
4. **Fix `_highlight_paused` URL→path mapping**; drive it from `location.scriptId` → server-resolved file, not deprecated `url`.
5. **Honest perf** — use `Performance.getMetrics` + `Memory.getDOMCounters`, compute FPS from real timestamps or drop it; delete `_perf_loop`.
6. **Single console path** — disable the inject `console.js` rewrite when CDP is connected (or gate on a status flag); drain `console_buffer` for the terminal fallback.
7. **Pause-aware eval** (`Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame`) + scope rendering + `setPauseOnExceptions` + `Page.reload`/`Page.captureScreenshot` — replaces the dead/weak features.
8. **Keybinding cleanup** per §5.
9. **Prune dead code** — unroute-able `handle_cdp_network_clear` (wire it or delete), `_terminal_reconnect`, `last_error` trim, `canvas_state`, `Timeline.eventRecorded`, `recording` toggle, redundant endpoints.
10. **Graceful fallback ladder** — Chrome absent → terminal console (exists); Chrome present but connect fails → actionable error + offer terminal fallback.
11. **Tests** — several tests currently *codify the bugs* (`set_breakpoint('sketch.js:42')` asserts the wrong URL is sent; FPS/perf tests assert the fake data). They must be updated to assert spec-correct behavior, and new tests added for the above.

Actually: Performance.metrics events fire ~1/s with `Timestamp` in microseconds (timeTicks?). The spec Metric has `Timestamp` value in microseconds since epoch? Actually `Timestamp` metric is in microseconds. We can compute FPS = 1000000/delta between two consecutive `Timestamp` values. That's a legit approximation of the frame/paint cadence? Not really FPS of rendering. Hmm. Honestly the cleanest honest approach: compute FPS client-side by injecting a rAF counter into the page? Overkill. Alternative: drop FPS sparkline and show "frame time" from `Frames` metric delta? The `Frames` metric is total frames painted. Delta of Frames per second = real FPS! `Frames` is a cumulative counter (total frames rendered). So `fps = frames_now - frames_prev` over the 1s between `Performance.metrics` events. That's honest real FPS. 
   - Add `Memory.enable` + `Memory.getDOMCounters` for nodes/listeners (real metric names: documents, nodes, jsEventListeners). Or just compute nodes via Performance `Nodes` metric (same value) and listeners via `JSEventListeners`. Simpler: use Performance domain metrics entirely: `Nodes` and `JSEventListeners` both exist in the metrics event. So `_handle_perf` can map `Nodes` → nodes, `JSEventListeners` → listeners, `JSHeapUsedSize` → heap, `Frames` delta → fps. Remove `_perf_loop` entirely (the Runtime.evaluate polling). Keep `Performance.enable` on connect.
   - Remove the `FPS`/`DOMNodes`/`EventListeners` dead names.

If the location matches a known script URL (exact or by suffix match against `_scripts` keys), use `Debugger.setBreakpoint` with scriptId, else `setBreakpointByUrl` with the exact URL. Return `locations` count + whether resolved, so the UI can report honestly.

Since it's already tested and the user wants full hardening with dedup... I'll wire it (route `DELETE /api/cdp/network`) and make Lua's `network_clear`/`D` call it.
   - Fix console double instrumentation: add an endpoint `/api/cdp/status` already exists; simplest dedupe: when CDP connected, ALSO drain console_buffer into the stream? No — the dedupe choice: keep inject as fallback, stop double instrumentation when CDP active. Approach: have the inject `console.js` check a global flag set by an endpoint before POSTing. Simplest robust: serve a tiny "am I CDP-connected" via `/api/cdp/status`; the console.js on each batch can check `window.__p5_cdp_active` which the server sets via injection at page-serve time? But the injection happens at serve time before connection. Alternative: The server injects console.js that first fetches `/api/cdp/status` once; if connected, skip rewriting console.* (CDP handles it). That introduces async timing. Cleaner: when CDP is connected, the server just doesn't need inject logs; but the page was already served with the rewrite. The inject POSTs still hit `/api/console/log` which buffers them. When CDP connected, `handle_cdp_stream` only drains CDP events, so inject logs accumulate and burst on disconnect.

If false, do the rewrite. That's a clean dedupe with a race caveat (page loads before connect). Good enough and honest. Also the server can suppress console_buffer draining duplication by having the console stream only used when not connected (already true).

But injection happens at serve time; if CDP connects after page load, stale. Combined approach: embed initial state + runtime re-check once. I'll go with the runtime fetch check (single fetch, cheap) and fall back to rewrite if fetch fails (graceful).
   - Prune `_terminal_reconnect`? That's Lua side. On server side nothing.
   - Fix `try_start_server` actual-port reporting: already returns actual port internally; Lua side needs to read it. Add the actual port into `/api/health` response (already returns? it returns server name + buffer size, not port). Add `"port"` to health JSON. Lua can parse server stdout line "Server running at http://localhost:PORT/" via on_stderr? It's on stdout, and server.lua jobstart only handles on_stderr. The auto-enable on connect — I'll keep auto-enable behavior but remove the unconditional auto-open in server.lua (gate it). Actually the user said make `cdp.enabled` real gate or remove. I'll keep it as an explicit gate but still allow explicit `:P5 cdp` to force-open (documenting "panel open auto-enables"). Hmm — keep current auto-enable on explicit open (documented), but server auto-open gated. That's the pragmatic path.

Implement: server `/api/cdp/perf/setRecording` or just have Lua skip storing when not recording. Simplest honest: when recording off, Lua still receives but stops appending; when on, resumes. That makes the toggle real on the display side. Fine.

7. Add endpoints wrappers: `C.pause_on_exceptions`, `C.reload`, `C.screenshot`, `C.pause`.
8. `C.close`: cleanup temp user-data-dir; don't kill user's Chrome (we launched with detach, killing would close user's browser if same profile — with user-data-dir it's our instance, so we *can* kill it on close? The user may want it to keep running. Keep: close the panel = close our Chrome instance since it's dedicated. I'll make it optional config `cdp.close_browser_on_close` default true).
9. `network_clear`/`D` → call server endpoint (`DELETE /api/cdp/network`) AND clear local.
10. `_terminal_auto_clear`: fix `last_error` logic — only trim if buffer has grown since last error or track last_error properly. Since it's always true now, gate the trim on an actual "last console activity" or remove the feature. Simplest honest: remove auto-clear entirely (the snack terminal has scrollback) OR keep trimming only when > N lines AND no recent errors — but there's no way to know errors in terminal mode. I'll remove the auto-clear (dead-ish) — but user said keep terminal fallback. Removing auto-trim is fine; the terminal has scrollback. Keep `_terminal_clear` keymap `c`.

Full hardening it is, with HUD keymaps kept-but-documented and the inject console retained as a deduped fallback. Here's the implementation plan.

## Implementation plan

### A. `server.py`
1. **Config plumbing** — add `--cdp-port` to `_parse_config`; drive `CONFIG['cdp']['remote_debugging_port']` from it.
2. **Honest performance** — rewrite `_handle_perf` to map real Performance-domain metric names: `JSHeapUsedSize`→heap, `Nodes`→nodes, `JSEventListeners`→listeners, and compute **FPS from the `Frames` counter delta** between `Performance.metrics` events (~1/s cadence). Delete the fake `fps: 60` fallback and the entire `_perf_loop` (`Runtime.evaluate` polling) — the Performance domain already emits the data.
3. **Breakpoints** — `set_breakpoint`: resolve bare filenames against `_scripts` (exact-URL → scriptId); if matched, use `Debugger.setBreakpoint` by scriptId; else `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` with the resolved exact `sourceURL`. Return `{ resolved = #locations, breakpointId }` so the UI can report honestly instead of "set" on an empty `locations`.
4. **New CDP features (genuinely useful for sketches)**:
   - `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` — track last paused `callFrameId`; `/api/cdp/evaluate` routes through it when paused (locals inspection), else `Runtime.evaluate`.
   - `/api/cdp/debug/pause` (`Debugger.pause`), `/api/cdp/debug/pauseExceptions` (`Debugger.setPauseOnExceptions`), `/api/cdp/page/reload` (`Page.reload`), `/api/cdp/page/screenshot` (`Page.captureScreenshot`, base64).
5. **Wire `/api/cdp/network` DELETE** (currently-routed-nowhere `handle_cdp_network_clear`) into `handle_cdp`; keep behavior.
6. **Prune** `Timeline.eventRecorded` branch; clear `pending_requests` on disconnect.
7. **Console dedupe** — `inject_scripts` embeds `window.__P5_CDP_ACTIVE` (connect state at serve time); `console.js` also re-checks once via `/api/cdp/status`; only rewrites `console.*` when CDP is *not* active. Graceful: on fetch failure, fall back to rewriting.

### B. `lua/p5/cdp.lua`
1. **Launch correctness** — add `--user-data-dir=<tempdir>` (track it) and `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1`; clean up tempdir on close; new config `cdp.close_browser_on_close` (default true) to kill our dedicated instance.
2. **Fix `_highlight_paused`** — replace the broken URL concatenation with basename matching against open buffers (`nvim_buf_get_name` tail vs `url` tail).
3. **Eval stuck-"pending"** — add `on_exit` to `C.eval`'s request marking entries failed.
4. **Recording toggle becomes real** — when `recording` is off, stop appending perf samples (display-side gate).
5. **New commands** — `C.pause`, `C.pause_on_exceptions`, `C.reload`, `C.screenshot`, bound to documented keys; Debug tab shows pause-exception state and resolved-breakpoint feedback.
6. **`network_clear`/`D`** — call `DELETE /api/cdp/network` (server-side clear) *and* clear local.
7. **`_terminal_auto_clear`** — remove the always-true trim (relies on the never-written `last_error`); keep manual `c` clear.
8. **`_terminal_reconnect`** — actually wire it into termopen `on_exit` (exit != 0) so the existing retry logic runs.
9. **`C.open` guard** — if `state.win` already valid, focus instead of spawning a duplicate panel.
10. **Keymaps** — keep the current HUD table unchanged; add an opt-out (`cdp.keymaps = false` skips `_set_keymaps`); document new keys.

### C. `lua/p5/server.lua`
1. Gate `vim.defer_fn(pcall(cdp.open), 500)` on `cdp.config.enabled` (and/or the autocmd) — stops the unconditional panel pop.
2. Pass `--cdp-port <n>` to `server.py`.
3. Capture the **actual bound port** from server stdout (`Server running at http://localhost:<real>/`) and update `S.port`, fixing the port-drift mismatch.

### D. `lua/p5/init.lua`
- Config additions: `cdp.keymaps = true`, `cdp.close_browser_on_close = true`; document `cdp.enabled` as the gate for server auto-open.

### E. `assets/inject/console.js`
- Status-aware rewrite per A.7.

### F. `lua/p5/commands.lua`
- Route `network_clear` through the server; add completions for `pause`, `pauseExceptions`, `reload`, `screenshot`.

### G. Docs
- `README.md` + `doc/p5-nvim.txt`: document the keymap table as **HUD-only** (with opt-out), honest perf semantics, new commands, and a troubleshooting entry for the Chrome-profile/`--user-data-dir` fix.

### H. Tests
- `test_cdp_client.py`: update breakpoint test to expect scriptId/exact-URL resolution; rewrite perf tests around real metric names + `Frames`-delta FPS; add tests for the new endpoints, `--cdp-port` parsing, network-clear routing, and evaluateOnCallFrame routing when paused.
- `cdp_spec.lua`: eval `on_exit`, highlight mapping, keymaps opt-out, open guard, network_clear endpoint call, terminal-reconnect wiring.
- Remove tests that currently *codify the bugs* (the `url='sketch.js'` assertion and fake-FPS assertions).

Ready to execute this once you approve. One note: the keymap "keep but document" choice means the `1`–`6` count-shadowing stays — I'll document it explicitly as a HUD-only caveat, but I'd still recommend `g1`-`g6` eventually if it bites anyone.

 class LiveReloadServer:
     """WebSocket server for live reload using asyncio."""
     
     def __init__(self, port: int, directory: str, file_watcher):
         self.port = port
         self.directory = directory
         self.file_watcher = file_watcher
         self.clients = set()
         self.server = None
     
     async def handler(self, websocket):
         """Handle WebSocket client connection."""
         self.clients.add(websocket)
         try:
             await websocket.send(json.dumps({"type": "connected", "message": "Live reload connected"}))
             await websocket.wait_closed()
         except (websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK, websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError):
             pass
         finally:
             self.clients.discard(websocket)
     
     async def start(self):
         """Start the WebSocket server."""
         for offset in range(10):
             try:
                 self.server = await websockets.serve(
                     self.handler, 'localhost', self.port + offset
                 )
                 if self.server.sockets:
                     self.port = self.server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
                 print(f"Live reload WebSocket running on ws://localhost:{self.port}")
                 return
             except OSError:
                 continue
         print("Warning: Could not start live reload server")
     
     async def broadcast(self, message: dict):
         """Broadcast message to all connected clients."""
         data = json.dumps(message)
         
         # Take a snapshot to avoid concurrent modification during iteration
         clients_snapshot = set(self.clients)
         disconnected = set()
         
         for client in clients_snapshot:
             try:
                 await client.send(data)
             except (websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK, websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError, websockets.exceptions.InvalidState):
                 disconnected.add(client)
             except Exception:
                 disconnected.add(client)
         
         for client in disconnected:
             self.clients.discard(client)
             try:
                 await client.close()
             except Exception:
                 pass
     
     async def close(self):
         """Close the server and all connections."""
         for client in list(self.clients):
             try:
                 await client.close()
             except Exception:
                 pass
         self.clients.clear()
         if self.server:
             self.server.close()
             await self.server.wait_closed()
 
 
 class FileWatcher:
     """Async file watcher using asyncio."""
     
     def __init__(self, directory: str, extensions: list, exclude_dirs: list, debounce_ms: int):
         self.directory = directory
         self.extensions = extensions
         self.exclude_dirs = exclude_dirs
         self.debounce_ms = debounce_ms / 1000
         self.last_trigger = 0
         self.running = False
         self._task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None
     
     def should_watch(self, path: str) -> bool:
         """Check if file should be watched."""
         path_obj = Path(path)
         
         # Check exclusion dirs
         for part in path_obj.parts:
             if part in self.exclude_dirs:
                 return False
         
         # Check extensions
         return any(str(path).endswith(ext) for ext in self.extensions)
     
     async def watch(self):
         """Watch for file changes - only trigger on actual file saves."""
         self.running = True
         last_mtimes = {}
         pending_changes = {}  # Track files that have changed but not yet stable
         
         while self.running:
             try:
                 current_mtimes = {}
                 for root, dirs, files in os.walk(self.directory):
                     dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in self.exclude_dirs]
                     
                     for file in files:
                         path = os.path.join(root, file)
                         if self.should_watch(path):
                             try:
                                 current_mtimes[path] = os.path.getmtime(path)
                             except OSError:
                                 continue
                 
                 now = datetime.now().timestamp()
                 
                 # Check for actual file changes (mtime differs from last known)
                 for path, mtime in current_mtimes.items():
                     last_mtime = last_mtimes.get(path)
                     
                     if last_mtime is None:
                         # First time seeing this file - skip
                         continue
                     
                     if mtime != last_mtime:
                         # File has changed - mark as pending
                         if path not in pending_changes:
                             pending_changes[path] = now
                 
                 # Check pending changes for stability
                 for path, change_time in list(pending_changes.items()):
                     current_mtime = current_mtimes.get(path)
                     last_mtime = last_mtimes.get(path)
                     
                     if current_mtime is None:
                         # File was deleted
                         del pending_changes[path]
                         continue
                     
                     if current_mtime == last_mtime and (now - change_time) >= self.debounce_ms:
                         # File is stable (not changing) and has been stable long enough
                         del pending_changes[path]
                         if now - self.last_trigger > self.debounce_ms:
                             self.last_trigger = now
                             yield path
                 
                 last_mtimes = current_mtimes
                 await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
                 
             except Exception as e:
                 print(f"File watcher error: {e}")
                 await asyncio.sleep(1)
     
     def start(self, callback):
         """Start the file watcher."""
         self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run_watcher(callback))
     
     async def _run_watcher(self, callback):
         """Run the watcher loop."""
         async for path in self.watch():
             await callback(path)
     
     async def stop(self):
         """Stop the file watcher."""
         self.running = False
         if self._task:
             self._task.cancel()
             try:
                 await self._task
             except asyncio.CancelledError:
                 pass

         """Handle incoming HTTP client request."""
         try:
             # Read request line
             request_line = await reader.readline()
             if not request_line:
                 writer.close()
                 await writer.wait_closed()
                 return
             
             request_line = request_line.decode().strip()
             
             # Parse request

                 if not line or line == b'\r\n':
                     break
                 header = line.decode().strip()
                 if ':' in header:
                     key, value = header.split(':', 1)
                     headers[key.strip().lower()] = value.strip()

             if method == 'POST' and path == '/api/console/log':
                 await self.handle_console_log(reader, writer, headers)
             elif method == 'GET' and path == '/api/console/stream':
                 await self.handle_console_stream(reader, writer, headers)
             elif method == 'GET' and path == '/api/health':
                 await self.handle_health(writer)

                 await self.handle_cdp(method, path, reader, writer, headers)

                 await self.handle_static(method, path, reader, writer, headers)

     async def handle_cdp_evaluate(self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter, headers: dict):
         if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
             await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
             return
         content_length = int(headers.get('content-length', 0))
         body = await reader.read(content_length)
         try:
             data = json.loads(body.decode())
             expr = data.get('expression', '')
             dangerous = ['file://', ' require(', "require('", 'require("', 'process.env', 'global.', '__dirname']
             for pat in dangerous:
                 if pat in expr:
                     await self._json_error(writer, 400, f'Rejected: expression contains forbidden pattern "{pat}"')
                     return
             result = await self.cdp_client.evaluate(expr)
             await self._json_response(writer, result)
         except Exception as e:
             await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

             writer.write(b'Content-Type: text/plain\r\n')
             writer.write(b'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *\r\n')
             writer.write(b'Connection: close\r\n')
             writer.write(b'\r\n')
             writer.write(b'File not found')
             await writer.drain()
             return
         
         # Determine content type
         ext = os.path.splitext(file_path)[1].lower()
         mime_types = {
             '.html': 'text/html',

         }

input.newString:
def _resolve_script(self, name):
        """Find scriptId for a bare filename (exact match or URL basename)."""
        if not name:
            return None
        if name in self._scripts:
            return self._scripts[name]
        tail = name.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
        for url, sid in self._scripts.items():
            if url.rsplit('/', 1)[-1] == tail:
                return sid
        return None

    async def evaluate(self, expression: str):
        if self._paused_frame_id:
            return await self.send_command('Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame', {
                'callFrameId': self._paused_frame_id,
                'expression': expression,
                'returnByValue': True,
                'includeCommandLineAPI': True,
            })
        return await self.send_command('Runtime.evaluate', {
            'expression': expression,
            'returnByValue': True,
            'includeCommandLineAPI': True,
        })

    async def set_breakpoint(self, location: str):
        parts = location.rsplit(':', 1)
        if len(parts) != 2:
            raise ValueError("Use format: file.js:line")
        url, line = parts[0], int(parts[1])
        sid = self._resolve_script(url)
        if sid:
            result = await self.send_command('Debugger.setBreakpoint', {
                'location': {'scriptId': sid, 'lineNumber': line - 1},
            })
            result['resolved'] = 1 if result.get('actualLocation') else 0
            return result
        result = await self.send_command('Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl', {
            'url': url,
            'lineNumber': line - 1,
        })
        result['resolved'] = len(result.get('locations', []))
        return result

    async def resume(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.resume')

    async def step_over(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.stepOver')

    async def step_into(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.stepInto')

    async def step_out(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.stepOut')

    async def pause(self):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.pause')

    async def set_pause_on_exceptions(self, state: str):
        await self.send_command('Debugger.setPauseOnExceptions', {'state': state})

    async def reload_page(self):
        await self.send_command('Page.reload')

    async def capture_screenshot(self):
        return await self.send_command('Page.captureScreenshot', {'format': 'png'})

async def handle_cdp_debug_pause(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        try:
            await self.cdp_client.pause()
            await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'pausing'})
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions(self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter, headers: dict):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        content_length = int(headers.get('content-length', 0))
        body = await reader.read(content_length)
        try:
            data = json.loads(body.decode())
            state = data.get('state', 'none')
            await self.cdp_client.set_pause_on_exceptions(state)
            await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'pause_on_exceptions=' + state})
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_page_reload(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        try:
            await self.cdp_client.reload_page()
            await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'reloading'})
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_page_screenshot(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if not self.cdp_client or not self.cdp_client.connected:
            await self._json_error(writer, 503, 'CDP not connected')
            return
        try:
            result = await self.cdp_client.capture_screenshot()
            await self._json_response(writer, result)
        except Exception as e:
            await self._json_error(writer, 400, str(e))

    async def handle_cdp_network_clear(self, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter):
        if self.cdp_client:
            self.cdp_client.clear_network_log()
        await self._json_response(writer, {'status': 'cleared'})

def test_debugger_resumed(self):
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Debugger.resumed', 'params': {}}))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 1)
        self.assertEqual(events[0][1]['event'], 'resumed')

    def test_debugger_resumed_clears_paused_frame(self):
        self.c._paused_frame_id = 'frame-1'
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Debugger.resumed', 'params': {}}))
        self.assertIsNone(self.c._paused_frame_id)

    def test_debugger_paused_tracks_frame_id(self):
        params = {
            'callFrames': [
                {'callFrameId': 'frame-1', 'functionName': 'draw',
                 'url': 'sketch.js', 'location': {'lineNumber': 3, 'columnNumber': 0}},
            ],
            'reason': 'breakpoint',
        }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message({'method': 'Debugger.paused', 'params': params}))
        self.assertEqual(self.c._paused_frame_id, 'frame-1')

    def test_perf_metrics_real_names_and_fps_delta(self):
        def metrics_event(frames, nodes, listeners, heap):
            return {
                'method': 'Performance.metrics',
                'params': {'metrics': [
                    {'name': 'Frames', 'value': frames},
                    {'name': 'Nodes', 'value': nodes},
                    {'name': 'JSEventListeners', 'value': listeners},
                    {'name': 'JSHeapUsedSize', 'value': heap},
                ]},
            }
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message(metrics_event(1000, 42, 7, 1048576)))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        self.assertEqual(len(events), 0, "first sample has no Frames delta")
        asyncio.run(self.c._handle_message(metrics_event(1060, 44, 8, 2097152)))
        events = self.c.drain_events()
        etype, data = events[0]
        self.assertEqual(etype, 'perf')
        self.assertEqual(data['fps'], 60)
        self.assertEqual(data['nodes'], 44)
        self.assertEqual(data['listeners'], 8)
        self.assertEqual(data['heap'], 2097152)

def test_handle_cdp_debug_step_out_no_client(self):

        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_debug_step_out(w))
        written = b''.join(c[0][0] for c in w.write.call_args_list if isinstance(c[0][0], bytes))
        self.assertIn(b'503', written)

    def test_handle_cdp_debug_pause_no_client(self):
        w = self._make_writer()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_debug_pause(w))
        written = b''.join(c[0][0] for c in w.write.call_args_list if isinstance(c[0][0], bytes))
        self.assertIn(b'503', written)

    def test_handle_cdp_debug_pause_with_client(self):
        self.server.cdp_client = MagicMock()
        self.server.cdp_client.connected = True
        self.server.cdp_client.pause = AsyncMock()
        w = self._make_writer()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_debug_pause(w))
        self.server.cdp_client.pause.assert_called_once()

    def test_handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions_no_client(self):
        w = self._make_writer()
        reader = AsyncMock()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions(reader, w, {'content-length': '0'}))
        written = b''.join(c[0][0] for c in w.write.call_args_list if isinstance(c[0][0], bytes))
        self.assertIn(b'503', written)

    def test_handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions_with_client(self):
        self.server.cdp_client = MagicMock()
        self.server.cdp_client.connected = True
        self.server.cdp_client.set_pause_on_exceptions = AsyncMock()
        w = self._make_writer()
        body = json.dumps({'state': 'uncaught'})
        headers = {'content-length': str(len(body))}
        reader = AsyncMock()
        reader.read.return_value = body.encode()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions(reader, w, headers))
        self.server.cdp_client.set_pause_on_exceptions.assert_called_once_with('uncaught')

    def test_handle_cdp_page_reload_no_client(self):
        w = self._make_writer()

        written = b''.join(c[0][0] for c in w.write.call_args_list if isinstance(c[0][0], bytes))
        self.assertIn(b'503', written)

    def test_handle_cdp_page_reload_with_client(self):
        self.server.cdp_client = MagicMock()
        self.server.cdp_client.connected = True
        self.server.cdp_client.reload_page = AsyncMock()
        w = self._make_writer()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_page_reload(w))
        self.server.cdp_client.reload_page.assert_called_once()

    def test_handle_cdp_page_screenshot_no_client(self):
        w = self._make_writer()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_page_screenshot(w))
        written = b''.join(c[0][0] for c in w.write.call_args_list if isinstance(c[0][0], bytes))
        self.assertIn(b'503', written)

    def test_handle_cdp_page_screenshot_with_client(self):
        self.server.cdp_client = MagicMock()
        self.server.cdp_client.connected = True
        self.server.cdp_client.capture_screenshot = AsyncMock(return_value={'data': 'aGVsbG8='})
        w = self._make_writer()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp_page_screenshot(w))
        self.server.cdp_client.capture_screenshot.assert_called_once()

    def test_handle_cdp_routes_network_clear(self):
        self.server.cdp_client = MagicMock()
        self.server.cdp_client.connected = True
        self.server.cdp_client.clear_network_log = MagicMock()
        w = self._make_writer()
        reader = AsyncMock()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp('DELETE', '/api/cdp/network', reader, w, {}))
        self.server.cdp_client.clear_network_log.assert_called_once()

    def test_handle_cdp_routes_pause(self):
        self.server.cdp_client = MagicMock()
        self.server.cdp_client.connected = True
        self.server.cdp_client.pause = AsyncMock()
        w = self._make_writer()
        reader = AsyncMock()
        asyncio.run(self.server.handle_cdp('POST', '/api/cdp/debug/pause', reader, w, {}))
        self.server.cdp_client.pause.assert_called_once()

parts.text:
## Goal
- Harden the p5.nvim CDP integration against the official Chrome DevTools Protocol spec: fix fake broken features (FPS, breakpoints, pause-highlight), prune dead code, add useful debugging capabilities, document HUD keymaps, and commit/push each phase.

## Constraints & Preferences
- User approved "All of it (full hardening)" — fixes 1–11 from the assessment.
- Keymaps: **Keep but document** — keep current HUD keymap table (incl. `1`–`6` tab switch), add opt-out config, document as HUD-only.
- Console: **Keep inject-based console as fallback, dedupe** — stop double instrumentation when CDP is active.
- Commit each phase when done and push when done.

## Progress
### Done
- Full assessment done (CDP conformance, loopholes, keybindings, fix plan) — presented and approved.
- **Phase A (`server.py`) — partial:**
  - `_parse_config`: added `--cdp-port` flag → `cfg['cdp']['remote_debugging_port']`.
  - `CDPClient.__init__`: replaced `_perf_metrics`/`_perf_task` with `_paused_frame_id` and `_perf_prev` (Frames-delta).
  - Deleted fake `_perf_loop` (Runtime.evaluate polling) entirely; removed `_perf_task` cancel from `disconnect`; added `pending_requests.clear()` + `_paused_frame_id=None` on disconnect.
  - `evaluate`: routes via `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` when `_paused_frame_id` set, else `Runtime.evaluate`.
  - `set_breakpoint`: `_resolve_script()` matches bare filename → exact URL in `_scripts` or URL-basename match → `Debugger.setBreakpoint` by scriptId; else `setBreakpointByUrl` with exact URL; sets `result['resolved']` = 0/1 (scriptId path) or `len(locations)` (URL path).
  - New CDPClient methods: `pause`, `set_pause_on_exceptions(state)`, `reload_page`, `capture_screenshot`.
  - `_handle_perf` rewritten with real metric names: `JSHeapUsedSize`→heap, `Nodes`→nodes, `JSEventListeners`→listeners, `Frames` cumulative counter delta per ~1s event → real FPS (clamped 0–1000); removed `_perf_metrics.append`.
  - `_handle_paused`: now stores `self._paused_frame_id = frames_raw[0].get('callFrameId')` and adds `scriptId` to per-frame dicts.
  - Removed dead `Timeline.eventRecorded: pass` branch; merged `Debugger.resumed` handler to also clear `_paused_frame_id` (fixed a duplicated unreachable elif).
  - `handle_cdp` routing: added `POST /api/cdp/debug/pause`, `POST /api/cdp/debug/pauseExceptions`, `POST /api/cdp/page/reload`, `GET /api/cdp/page/screenshot`, and wired `DELETE /api/cdp/network` (the previously unrouted `handle_cdp_network_clear`).
  - `HTTPServer` handlers added: `handle_cdp_debug_pause`, `handle_cdp_debug_pause_exceptions`, `handle_cdp_page_reload`, `handle_cdp_page_screenshot`; existing `handle_cdp_network_clear` retained as the DELETE handler.

### In Progress
- Phase A (`server.py`) — remaining items: console dedupe via inject scripts/status (server-side part), verify remaining `_perf_metrics` references are gone, run pytest.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Key Decisions
- FPS computed honestly from `Performance.metrics` `Frames` counter delta (matches CDP spec) instead of fake `fps: 60`.
- Breakpoints resolved client-side (server) against `scriptParsed` URL map for exact `sourceURL`/scriptId — fixes V8 exact-match `setBreakpointByUrl` failure confirmed in `v8-debugger-agent-impl.cc`.
- Pause-aware eval via `Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame` top frame.
- Keep current HUD keymap table per user choice; add `cdp.keymaps` opt-out + docs only.
- Inject console stays as no-Chrome fallback; dedupe when CDP active.

## Next Steps
1. Finish `server.py` Phase A: console dedupe (embed CDP-active state; console.js checks `/api/cdp/status` and skips rewriting when connected), confirm no stale `_perf_metrics` refs, run `pytest` (update `tests/test_cdp_client.py` first — breakpoint/perf tests encode old buggy behavior).
2. Commit Phase A; push.
3. Phase B `lua/p5/cdp.lua`: Chrome `--user-data-dir` + `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1` + tempdir cleanup; fix `_highlight_paused` basename matching (broken `url_path` concatenation bug); eval `on_exit` marks pending failure; recording toggle gates samples; new commands (pause, pauseExceptions, reload, screenshot); wire network_clear to DELETE endpoint; wire `_terminal_reconnect`; remove always-true `_terminal_auto_clear`; open guard for existing win; `cdp.keymaps=false` opt-out.
4. Commit Phase B; push.
5. Phase C `lua/p5/server.lua`: gate `cdp.open()` on `cdp.config.enabled`; pass `--cdp-port`; capture actual bound port from stdout (fixes port-drift mismatch).
6. Phase D `lua/p5/init.lua`: add `cdp.keymaps`, `cdp.close_browser_on_close` config; document.
7. Phase E `assets/inject/console.js`: status-aware console.* rewrite.
8. Phase F `lua/p5/commands.lua`: route network_clear via server; new subcommand completions.
9. Phase G docs (README.md + doc/p5-nvim.txt): HUD keymap table as HUD-only, new commands, troubleshooting for Chrome profile/`--user-data-dir`.
10. Phase H tests: update `tests/test_cdp_client.py` and `tests/p5/cdp_spec.lua` to spec-correct expectations; run pytest + luacheck/stylua; final commit + push.

## Critical Context
- **V8 fact**: `Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl` `url` matches script `sourceURL()` EXACTLY (`script.sourceURL() == selector_` in `v8-debugger-agent-impl.cc`), so old `url="sketch.js"` never resolved against `http://localhost:8000/sketch.js`.
- Chrome launch without `--user-data-dir` fails to expose debug port if an existing Chrome instance is running — the top user-facing launch bug.
- `server.py` port-drift: binds `port + offset` on contention but Lua stores requested port.
- Old `_highlight_paused` bug: `url:match("://[^/]+(/.*)") .. fnamemodify(url,":t")` double-appends basename → `sketch.jssketch.js`.
- `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` + inject console.js double-instrumentation: console.js fetch-POSTs to `/api/console/log` never drained while CDP connected.
- Duplicate-elif bug in `_message_loop` fixed (two `Debugger.resumed` branches; second was unreachable).
- `handle_cdp_network_clear` was defined + unit-tested but never routed.

## Relevant Files
- `server.py`: CDP client + HTTP proxy; Phase A changes (config, perf, breakpoints, new endpoints).
- `lua/p5/cdp.lua`: Lua CDP panel, keymaps, terminal fallback; Phase B target.
- `lua/p5/server.lua`: server launcher; Phase C target (gate, --cdp-port, port capture).
- `lua/p5/init.lua`: config (add `cdp.keymaps`, `cdp.close_browser_on_close`).
- `lua/p5/commands.lua`: `:P5 cdp` subcommands (network_clear routing, new completions).
- `assets/inject/console.js`: console rewrite fallback; needs CDP-status dedupe.
- `assets/inject/livereload.js`: unaffected.
- `tests/test_cdp_client.py`: Python CDP tests — encode old buggy breakpoint/perf/etc.; must be updated.
- `tests/p5/cdp_spec.lua`: Lua CDP specs — must be updated (eval on_exit, highlight, opt-outs).
- `README.md`, `doc/p5-nvim.txt`: docs for Phase G.

 C._start_sse_job = function()
 	if C.state.job_id then
 		return
 	end
 	if not check_curl() then
 		return
 	end
 	local url = string.format("http://localhost:%d/api/cdp/stream", C.state.port)
 	C.state.job_id = vim.fn.jobstart({ "curl", "-s", "-N", "--max-time", "3600", url }, {
 		on_stdout = function(_, data)
 			if not data then
 				return
 			end
 			local buf = C.state.sse_buffer or ""
 			for _, chunk in ipairs(data) do
 				buf = buf .. (chunk or "")
 			end
 			local lines = vim.split(buf, "\n", { plain = true })
 			C.state.sse_buffer = table.remove(lines) or ""
 			for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
 				if line ~= "" then
 					local ok, ev = pcall(vim.json.decode, line)
 					if ok then
 						vim.schedule(function()
 							C._on_event(ev)
 						end)
 					end
 				end
 			end
 		end,
 		on_exit = function()
 			vim.schedule(function()
 				C.state.job_id = nil
 				C.state.sse_buffer = ""
 				if C.state.buf and is_buf(C.state.buf) and C.state.connected then
 					notify("CDP stream disconnected, reconnecting...", "info")
 					vim.defer_fn(function()
 						C._start_sse_job()
 					end, 1000)
 				end
 			end)
 		end,
 	})
 end
